brdQuote: Hiring target preserves the application and accepted-offer origin of an employee; no repeated conversion.
exists: Uniqueness is only per offer or application. In db/migrations/0034_hiring.sql, hiring_handover (lines 553-576) is unique on offer_id, application_id and employee_id, and hiring_offer_one_live (line 473) is per application. apps/api/src/modules/hiring/offer.ts recordResponse (lines 229-250) checks only that the requisition is APPROVED, the application is at OFFER and the requisition still has vacancies. apps/api/src/modules/hiring/handover.ts handOver (lines 71-75) checks only this offer's handover, the ACCEPTED state, the APPROVED requisition and the OFFER stage. Neither looks at the candidate: its other ACCEPTED offers, an earlier handover, or candidate.state. missing: A candidate who applies to two approved requisitions (FR-013 allows this) can have both offers recorded ACCEPTED and both handed over, giving two DRAFT employees for one person. Needed: under a candidate-level lock, refuse acceptance or handover while the candidate (or a record confirmed as its duplicate) has another ACCEPTED offer, or has a handover to an employee who is not separated or archived. brdQuote: identify invalid or repeated punches
exists: Replay control works by event key only: the unique index attendance_punch_event_uq (0008_attendance.sql lines 86-87) is on company, source_identity_key and external_event_key. importPunches (service.ts lines 46-64) counts an identical replay of the same key as a duplicate and a changed payload under the same key as CONFLICTING_DUPLICATE_KEY. The only other checks are unparseable or offset-less timestamps (lines 35-37) and unknown or out-of-scope employees (lines 39-45). evaluate.ts pair() (lines 75-92) turns two INs into MISSING_OUT_PUNCH.
missing: A repeated punch (same employee, instant and direction) under a different event key is stored as a second, permanent punch and never identified as repeated. This happens when a row appears twice in one file, when a punch is re-entered by hand, or when another source delivers it again. The day then evaluates to EXCEPTION 'MISSING_OUT_PUNCH' or 'MISSING_IN_PUNCH', which hides the real cause and can only be fixed by an amendment. Punches dated in the future are accepted as valid. Needed: during manual import, report a row identical to a stored punch, or repeated earlier in the batch, as REPEATED_PUNCH instead of storing it; flag repeats that arrive from a different source; reject instants later than the submission time as invalid; add API tests. How flagged cross-source repeats are paired stays under the approval FR-020 requires for pairing rules.

DF05 (line 4931) makes Monday-Friday only the default and says 'Shift and holiday calendars are editable and effective-dated'; FR-005 (line 439) asks for maintained 'location-specific holidays and weekly-off patterns'. exists: db/migrations/0035_appraisal.sql: appraisal_entry holds only self_score/self_comment and manager_score/manager_comment per goal; appraisal_revision holds self_comment, manager_comment and weighted_result. A reviewer confirmation (apps/api/src/modules/appraisal/review.ts decideAppraisal) records only APPROVE/RETURN plus an optional private remark in approval_decision.reason. docs/03 I-24 says 'no separate reviewer score is stored'. The DF04 wave-2 minimum form contract (BRD line 4925) lists 'appraisal(employee, cycle, weighted goals, self/manager/reviewer scores, status, restricted comments)' and adds that child entities must exist 'before the matching feature is marked built'.
missing: The database has no column or table for reviewer ratings, so FR-043's three separate ratings and the DF04 'reviewer scores' cannot be kept. The owner must decide: per-goal or overall reviewer score; whether level-1 and level-2 reviewers each score; whether a reviewer score changes the final rating, which F1 defines as the weighted manager result. Then build: storage, entry on the confirm decision, confidential 'rating'-group reads in the staff view, report and export, and the web review form.

brdQuote: Level 1 completes at manager approval; level 2 remains pending until reviewer decision
exists: apps/api/src/modules/appraisal/registration.ts always routes 'appraisal' through step 1 (DIRECT_MANAGER, appraisal.rate.rating) and then step 2 (HR_FALLBACK_LIST, appraisal.confirm.rating). approval_levels = 2 adds a third decision through 'appraisal_second_review'. review.ts complete() runs only after a reviewer confirms. Test 'a second reviewer level applies only where the cycle sets it explicitly' (appraisal-flow.api.test.ts) records three decisions for level 2. This follows docs/03 I-24's reading of F1 ('Manager rates then an independent assigned eligible reviewer confirms. One reviewer step is the default').
missing: With the default approval_levels = 1, an appraisal is not complete at the manager's approval: an HR-list reviewer must also confirm. The FR-043 acceptance and BR-013 (BRD line 1715: 'one-level manager review or two-level manager and manager's-manager review') read level 1 as manager only, and level 2 as manager plus the manager's manager. The code instead sends level 2 to the HR fallback list. The FR-043 acceptance test as written would fail. The owner must choose a reading: (a) level 1 = manager only, level 2 = manager plus an independent second reviewer (manager's manager or explicit list); or (b) keep I-24 and amend the acceptance criterion. Option (a) needs workflow re-provisioning (access/provision.ts) for existing companies.

brdQuote: Provide KRA Setting, KRA Review, View KRASetting and upload.
exists: Goals are set only by HR or the direct manager with appraisal.manage: POST /v1/appraisals and PUT /v1/appraisals/:id/goals (apps/api/src/modules/appraisal/appraisals.ts createAppraisal/replaceGoals), or by the HR upload APPRAISAL_GOALS_V1 (goal-import.ts). Goals become usable for self-entry at once. appraisal_item (0035) has no submission or review state. No goal-review transaction kind or task exists, and there is no employee goal-proposal route. docs/03 I-23 says 'there is no separate KRA approval step'.
missing: No KRA Setting Review exists (CL-125). The FR-041 acceptance ('mode 1 awaits manager review') and F1 (BRD line 5079: 'upload creates DRAFT and never silently substitutes for human approval') both assume goals receive a human approval. FR-060 (BRD line 1099) also lists 'goal' tasks in the unified queue. Today an HR upload sets goals that no manager or employee ever approves before self-entry and rating. The owner must decide who proposes KRAs (employee, manager or HR) and who reviews them. Then build: goal submission and review states, a review task routed to the manager, queue entries, and web screens.

brdQuote: Manual or formula-based target rating is configured
exists: appraisal_setting (0035) holds only cycle_start_month; appraisal_cycle has no rating-method field. review.ts decideAppraisal always computes weighted_result = sum(weight × manager score)/100, and complete() copies it into final_rating. The E11 'Rating method' setting (BRD line 2017) has no counterpart. docs/03 I-23/I-24 and docs/06 do not mention manual mode; they record only competencies, sections and the employee-visible result as blocked.
missing: The FR-042 acceptance (BRD line 885: 'When manual mode is enabled users enter permitted ratings; formula mode produces the approved test score') cannot be tested, because the rating method cannot be configured and only the formula path exists. The owner must confirm whether a manual mode is wanted and what it means: a directly entered overall rating, its permitted values, and whether it replaces or sits beside the F1 weighted result. That decision should then be recorded in docs/03 or built as a cycle/company setting.

brdQuote: historical entries retain the original classification
exists: Lines copy the activity's productive flag when entered (sheets.ts insertLine/updateOwnLine), and reports and utilisation read l.productive (reports.ts). Activities can be reclassified through PATCH /v1/timesheet/activities/:id with productive (masters.ts updateActivity); masters can be renamed or have their periods changed. The timesheet tests cover deactivating an activity or job-activity link, and the database guard that stops a job changing project. No test reclassifies an activity's productive flag after lines are approved.
missing: Add a test: approve a week, flip the activity's productive flag and rename the job, then confirm that the approved lines, the hours report's productiveMinutes and utilisationPercent are unchanged, and that a newly entered line takes the new flag.

brdQuote: Recovery does not exceed outstanding balance
exists: Loans (apps/api/src/modules/payroll-outputs/loans.ts, db/migrations/0046_payroll_loans.sql) store principal, schedule and recovered_amount. An instalment reaches payroll only as an ordinary approved INPUT on the loan's recovery DEDUCTION head: inputs.ts checkLines accepts any positive amount on any INPUT head, and payroll/calculate.ts has no loan awareness at all. After a run is locked, a manual call (POST /v1/payroll-outputs/runs/:id/loan-recoveries, loans.ts recognizeRecoveries) recognises a line only if the loan is DISBURSED and the line is within the outstanding balance; otherwise it only reports RECOVERY_EXCEEDS_OUTSTANDING and recognises nothing, not even in part. loans.api.test.ts lines 280-295 processes and locks a 1,500 deduction against a 1,000 balance and only asserts that it is reported.
missing: The salary deduction itself is never limited. A locked run can deduct more than the outstanding balance, or deduct on the recovery head whatever the loan's state (e.g. before disbursement). The employee is over-deducted with no correction path (adjustments are not built), and the loan balance shown, including in the settlement view ('settlement shows remaining balance'), stays wrong until someone runs recognition by hand. Needed: (1) a blocking calculation exception, or a check at input approval, when a live loan's recovery-head line exceeds its outstanding balance net of recoveries already processed but not yet recognised; (2) refuse such deductions when no DISBURSED loan stands behind the head; (3) run recognition as part of processing, or at least before the next calculation; (4) optionally report due instalments that were not entered.

brdQuote: collect approved eligible input revisions
exists: Inputs are immutable lines inside a batch. payroll_input_batch states are DRAFT/SUBMITTED/APPROVED/REJECTED/CANCELLED, and hrms_payroll_input_guard forbids edits (0043_payroll.sql). cancelBatch (inputs.ts:444) cancels only DRAFT or SUBMITTED batches. Salary stops have a revoke route (POST /payroll/salary-stops/:id/revoke); input batches have no revoke or replace route in payroll/routes.ts. calculateChunk step 7 (calculate.ts:383-395) takes every APPROVED, unconsumed input of the period.
missing: There is no input revision model and no controlled reversal of an approved input that has not yet been used by a run. DF03 (line 4913) says 'Approved changes need a controlled reversal/cancellation action'. A wrong approved line (bad amount, or a duplicate under a new reference) is paid by the next calculation. Returning the run does not drop it. Excluding the employee and paying them in another run of the same period picks up the same input again. Needed: revoke an approved batch (or line) with a reason, by someone independent of the preparer, before any calculation snapshot has taken it (same pattern as revokeStop: lockServiceMonth plus snapshotTaken). The revocation frees its references, is audited and notified, and a corrected batch can optionally supersede it.

brdQuote: Employees may access only their own issued payroll/tax outputs and permitted private ESS records through an explicit Employee OWN assignment.
exists: The payroll core never shows the caller's own record in an Admin context. runs.ts runRecords filters out the linked employee; recordDetail, stopDetail, holdDetail, listHolds, listStops, loanDetail, previewPayslip and outputFile all call assertNotSelf. The outputs reads do not. (1) payroll-outputs/reports.ts registerRecords, behind GET /v1/payroll-outputs/runs/:id/register and the PAYROLL_REGISTER export in report/catalogue.ts, lists the caller's own record with earnings, deductions, net, held, reserved and paid: registerScope returns 'true' for an unrestricted grant and nothing filters out the own record. (2) bank.ts recordPayment (GET /v1/payroll-outputs/records/:id/payment) calls only assertInScope and returns the caller's own earned/held/reserved/paid, with each hold's kind, state and amount. (3) bank.ts batchLines lists the caller's own bank line. report-exports.api.test.ts has no own-record case.
missing: An HR Administrator holding payroll_report.read/export or payroll_bank.read sees their own unissued payroll result, and the kind and amount of holds on their own salary, in the Admin context. This bypasses the Employee OWN route, which deliberately shows only issued payslips and status-only hold information (I-43). BRD line 4895 also says own records are reached by selecting the Employee context. Needed: apply the core's own-record rule to the register (JSON and export), the record payment position and the manifest lines (exclude or deny the linked employee), with tests.

brdQuote: salary-stop interpretation is explicit in the result and disbursement report
exists: The run result shows the stop: payroll_record.salary_stop_mode, salaryStopMode in runs.ts runRecords/recordDetail, and the SALARY_STOP_EXCLUDED and SALARY_STOP_HOLD warnings. The disbursement report (payroll-outputs/reports.ts disbursementTotals/disbursementReport, and the PAYROLL_DISBURSEMENT export) does not. It totals only CALCULATED frozen records, so employees under an EXCLUDE_CALCULATION stop are absent and uncounted. HOLD_DISBURSEMENT stop holds are merged into 'held' together with policy holds and bank safety blocks. The manifest's excluded summary (bank.ts plan: held, reservedOrPaid, nothingPayable, excludedByPreparer) has no stop category. The register rows and the PAYROLL_REGISTER export columns (reports.ts registerRecords, catalogue.ts) have no stop mode either.
missing: The disbursement report and its export (and the register) need to show the stop interpretation: (1) the count and amount withheld under HOLD_DISBURSEMENT stops, separate from other holds; (2) the employees excluded from calculation by EXCLUDE_CALCULATION stops, with count, list and mode; (3) a stop-mode column on register rows. The web disbursement view needs the same.

brdQuote: Produce employee-level exceptions, component totals and comparison with the prior period.
exists: runs.ts runComponents serves GET /v1/payroll/runs/:id/components, GET /v1/payroll-outputs/runs/:id/comparison and the PAYROLL_COMPARISON export. When every current member is in the caller's row scope, it compares against the full chunk totals of the latest earlier processed run of the same calendar and filters. It never checks the prior run's members against the caller's scope, and scope is judged on the current effective assignment (access/authorize.ts employeeScopePredicate).
missing: An Admin with a department, location or employee filter, whose scope covers this month's members, receives prior totals that include last month's members now outside their scope (transferred, or not in their employee list). Combined with priorNet for in-scope employees from runRecords, an out-of-scope employee's prior pay can be worked out by subtraction. This conflicts with C4 (line 4688: 'New list/read access uses current effective assignment'). Fix: require the prior runs to be wholly in scope (requireRunScope), otherwise fall back to the SCOPE basis over in-scope employees.

requirement: FR-031 (Appendix A CL-087 Upload Stop Salary)
brdQuote: past salary/TDS and salary stop instructions
exists: Salary stops can only be proposed one at a time (POST /v1/payroll/periods/:id/salary-stops, inputs.ts proposeStop). Payroll inputs (PAYROLL_INPUTS_V1) and loans (LOAN_REQUESTS_V1) have uploads. No salary-stop template or import exists.
missing: The observed 'Upload Stop Salary' input function (CL-087, BRD line 2613; listed for FR-028 to FR-039 and FR-064) is missing. Needed: a published, versioned template whose rows pass exactly proposeStop's rules (mode, active criterion, release criterion, reason, verified evidence document ids, one live stop per employee and period). The upload is malware-scanned, all-or-nothing and safe to repeat, and each stop is still decided independently.

requirement: FR-038 (Appendix A CL-094 Salary Progression Chart)
brdQuote: comparison, progression, JV, liability provisions
exists: payroll-outputs/reports.ts provides the register, disbursement and comparison reports (exports PAYROLL_REGISTER, PAYROLL_DISBURSEMENT, PAYROLL_COMPARISON). JV and statutory outputs return NOT_CONFIGURED. Nothing in the code or docs mentions 'progression', and docs/03 I-40 and I-45 (the open report questions) do not list it.
missing: There is no Salary Progression Chart output (BRD line 345; CL-094 says the page was not inspected). Its measure (CTC, gross or net), grouping (per employee or per group) and time span are undefined. The owner must define it; it can then be built from processed payroll records under payroll_report grants.

brdQuote: Policy may narrow these values through approved versioning.
exists: holds.ts hard-codes FIRST_ESCALATION_BUSINESS_DAYS = 2, ESCALATION_INTERVAL_BUSINESS_DAYS = 5 and a daily reminder for every unresolved hold. Hold criterion revisions in payroll_hold_criterion are versioned and activated by a second person, but they carry only max_review_days.
missing: No approved, versioned policy value can shorten the reminder or escalation intervals (for example, first escalation after 1 business day). Needed: optional interval fields on the hold criterion revision, never longer than the H2 defaults; copy them onto each hold and have runPayrollHoldReviews use them. Bank safety blocks keep the defaults.

brdQuote: Define interest and early-settlement rules if required.
exists: Loans are interest-free (I-32): loans.ts refuses any interestRate with INTEREST_NOT_CONFIGURED, and ownLoans returns earlySettlement NOT_CONFIGURED. A DISBURSED loan closes only when payroll recoveries equal the principal. No route records an early repayment, lump-sum recovery or waiver. docs/03 records only the interest interpretation (I-32) and the final-settlement payment question (I-40 item 2).
missing: The owner needs to set the early-settlement rule: repayment outside payroll, lump-sum recovery, waiver or write-off, and whether evidence and an independent approver are required. After that, a settlement event is needed that reduces the outstanding balance and closes the loan, with audit.

brdQuote: a receipt cannot be opened without access to its parent claim
exists: GET /expense/lines/:id/receipt (apps/api/src/modules/expense/routes.ts:103-136) requires only expense.view_receipt in the 'receipt' group plus row scope over the claimant (canAccessEmployee). It then serves any CLEAN receipt on any line, whatever the revision or claim state. receipts.api.test.ts:89 builds reviewerEng from the HR_ADMINISTRATOR default duties, which do not include expense.read.operational (EXPENSE_FINANCE_ADMIN is ceiling-only, access/baseline.ts:143-158,235,244-254), plus the receipt grant. Lines 157-165 then expect 200 for a receipt on a line of a never-submitted draft (receiptOnLine only drafts).
missing: There is no parent-claim check. The acting assignment does not need expense.read.operational on the claim, so the same user gets 403 on GET /expense/claims/:id but 200 on its receipts. Anyone but the claimant can also open receipts on unsubmitted drafts, or on claims they neither review nor pay. DF02 limits expense data to the claimant, assigned reviewers and payment operators. Fix: require claim read access on the same assignment, and for non-claimants a submitted revision. Add negative tests (receipt grant without claim read; draft receipt opened by a manager or HR).

brdQuote: allow the assigned eligible finance reviewer to decide reimbursable line amounts and final entitlement under approved policy
exists: assertIndependentReleaser (apps/api/src/modules/expense/service.ts:669-674) excludes only the instruction preparer, expense_obligation.approved_by and the claimant. approved_by is the user of the last APPROVE (service.ts:424-428), which on a claim above 50,000 is the high-value approver. preparePayment (579-637) has no independence check. recordOutcome (698-704) and reversePayment (732-733) return replays before any independence check.
missing: On a high-value claim, the finance reviewer who set every line amount (the FR-073 entitlement decision) is not excluded, so they can release, confirm and reverse the payment. The final approver, the finance-line approver or the claimant can prepare it. This conflicts with DF02 'Preparation, entitlement approval and payment release are distinct actors on a transaction' (line 4901) and DF07 'The entitlement approver cannot release its payment' (line 4959). Fix: exclude every decider of the approving instance, and the claimant, from prepare, release, outcome and reversal, and check independence before answering a replay. Payroll fixed the same class of defect as D-032 (docs/08_verification_log.md:459).

brdQuote: a reversal retains original evidence and cannot exceed its payment
exists: reversePayment (apps/api/src/modules/expense/service.ts:731-733) runs `select 1 from payment_event where event_key = $2` and treats any hit as a replay: a CONFIRMED or FAILED event, or an event on another instruction. It then returns 200 {replayed:true} without writing the reversal. preparePayment (580-583) returns whichever instruction already holds the idempotency key, even one for another claim or amount. Only recordOutcome checks that the key belongs to the same instruction (EVIDENCE_KEY_REUSED).
missing: Example: a reversal posted with the bank reference already used to confirm the payment (e.g. BANKREF-0001), or with another instruction's key, is silently dropped. Net paid, outstanding, payment_state and EXPENSE_REGISTER stay overstated while the caller sees success. A prepare that reuses a key for claim Y returns claim X's instruction and leaves Y unprepared. DF07 'Idempotent evidence keys and reversal bounds apply' (line 4961) means a replay must be the same request: same instruction, kind REVERSED and same amount for a reversal; same claim and amount for a preparation. Anything else should get 409 (EVIDENCE_KEY_REUSED or IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED).

brdQuote: require an authorised documented review before accepting a blocking match
exists: Submission sets the DUPLICATE_SUSPECTED, OVER_LIMIT, RECEIPT_MISSING and LATE_SUBMISSION flags and requires only the claimant's exception_reason (apps/api/src/modules/expense/service.ts:297-306). That reason is never returned: getClaim (527-531) omits exception_reason and invoice_reference. The reviewer screen (apps/web/src/pages/work.tsx ExpenseTask) shows only the flags, defaults the approved amount to the claimed amount, and asks for a reason only on reduction. The line-decision trigger (db/migrations/0012_expense_payment.sql:248-250) requires a reason only when allowed < claimed. Tests accept a flagged line explained only as 'n/a' (expense.api.test.ts:190).
missing: There is no authorised documented review. The financial reviewer can accept a duplicate-suspected, over-limit, late or receipt-less line at full amount without recording a clearance reason, and cannot even read the claimant's justification. So 'clearance retains its reason' (line 1281) is not met and DF06 'records a reason for reduction/rejection/exception' (line 4951) is not enforced. Fix: require a reviewer clearance reason for every flagged line accepted, enforced in the trigger as well, and show the claimant's reason to the assigned financial and high-value reviewers as a reason-classified group.

brdQuote: A missing required receipt, unsupported currency, ambiguous policy or unresolved duplicate exception blocks submission with a field or rule reason
exists: insertLines refuses a receipt only if it is already QUARANTINED when attached (apps/api/src/modules/expense/service.ts:53). A receipt saved while PENDING_SCAN is rescanned later by the worker (storage/scan.ts scanPendingAttachments, called from worker/scheduler.ts:97) and can become QUARANTINED. submitClaim computes receipt_missing as `not exists (expense_receipt ...)` with no scan_state condition (service.ts:266), and getClaim's receiptPresent does the same (530).
missing: A receipt quarantined after the draft was saved still satisfies the receipt requirement. There is no RECEIPT_MISSING flag and no exception reason, and reviewers see 'attached' while GET .../receipt answers 409 FILE_NOT_RELEASED. Finance can then approve a line with no usable evidence. Fix: treat a QUARANTINED receipt as missing at submission; at financial approval refuse or flag any line whose receipt is not CLEAN (as I-21 does for sensitive-change evidence); return the scan state to reviewers.

brdQuote: Repeating the same receipt or invoice creates a review exception
exists: The duplicate fingerprint is sha256(employee|expenseDate|category|claimedAmount|receipt checksum) (apps/api/src/modules/expense/service.ts:54-56), and receipt files are also matched company-wide by checksum (268-274). expense_line.invoice_reference is stored (59-62) but is used nowhere else in the API, SQL or web. getClaim does not return it, and the web form never sends it.
missing: Reuse of an invoice or bill reference is never detected. The same merchant invoice number on two claims, with a different scan, amount, date or employee, raises no DUPLICATE_SUSPECTED exception and can be approved twice. DF06 says 'matching an external claim/reference key cannot create duplicate entitlement' (line 4951). Fix: compare normalised merchant plus invoice reference against the lines of live submitted revisions company-wide, under the existing advisory locks, and flag both lines; add an index.

brdQuote: validate a claim against the approved eligibility, required receipts, expense policy and currency rules before submission
exists: The limit checks in submitClaim (apps/api/src/modules/expense/service.ts:252-264) work as follows. PER_DAY sums the same category and date across the revision and the employee's other live submitted claims. PER_NIGHT only compares one line's amount with limit x that line's own nights. The baseline ACCOMMODATION category is PER_NIGHT, limit 5,000 (access/baseline.ts:658).
missing: Nights are not grouped across lines. Two accommodation lines covering the same night are each within the limit and raise no OVER_LIMIT flag, whether in one claim or across live claims. Examples: 5,000 + 4,000 for the night of 20 Oct; or 2 nights for 10,000 from 20 Oct plus 1 night for 5,000 on 21 Oct. DF06 says 'Per-day/night grouping uses actual expense service date and declared nights' (line 4947). Fix: for each covered night (expense_date to expense_date+nights-1, claimed/nights), sum across the revision and the employee's other live submitted claims, under the existing employee lock.

brdQuote: use approved dated category policies, eligible employee classifications and decision routes, and retain the rules used for submitted claims
exists: The only expense policy routes are GET /expense/policies and POST /expense/policies/:id/activate (apps/api/src/modules/expense/routes.ts:304-319). Provisioning seeds DEFAULT revision 1 as a DRAFT with the DF06 limits (access/provision.ts:177-203); categories are seed-only. Migration 0012 has no freeze trigger on expense_policy or expense_policy_rule, unlike the leave (0007 hrms_leave_policy_frozen), attendance (0008) and confirmation (0009) policies. Activation (service.ts:760-772) does not check for overlap with another ACTIVE revision.
missing: Dated policy revisions cannot be configured through the API: limits, receipt requirement, grade/location rules, submission window, high-value threshold, end-dating and retirement, and categories. An ACTIVE policy's rules can also be updated in place, and expense_revision keeps only policy_id, so 'the rules used for submitted claims' are not reliably retained. Fix: draft-revision maintenance with independent activation, end-dating of the superseded revision, refusal of overlapping revisions, and freeze triggers on ACTIVE policies and their rules.

brdQuote: permit withdrawal only before committed final approval or payment
exists: withdrawClaim (apps/api/src/modules/expense/service.ts:460-467) allows only DRAFT and RETURNED claims. It takes no lockTransaction, cancels no approval, writes no audit and emits no event. Migration 0012 allows WITHDRAWN only from DRAFT or RETURNED (0012_expense_payment.sql:475-476). Leave withdrawal, by contrast, accepts SUBMITTED requests, cancels the active approval, writes an audit record and emits leave.withdrawn (leave/service.ts:375-410). The web 'My claims' table (apps/web/src/pages/work.tsx ExpensesPage) offers neither withdrawal nor correction of a returned claim.
missing: A claim pending manager, finance or high-value review cannot be withdrawn. FR-074 and DF03 ('Withdraw only before a final decision', line 4913) allow it, and the acceptance case of simultaneous withdrawal and final approval (line 1269) assumes it. Fix: add pending-to-WITHDRAWN transitions; serialise with decisions through lockTransaction plus cancelActiveApproval; audit the withdrawal and emit a withdrawn event; give the claimant UI to correct a RETURNED claim and to withdraw; test the race (one result, no obligation).

brdQuote: outcome notices under confirmed business rules
exists: submitClaim and decideExpense enqueue expense.submitted (payload claimId, taskId) and expense.decided (apps/api/src/modules/expense/service.ts:334-340, 448-456). The dispatcher's describe() has no expense case (notification/dispatcher.ts:70-268), and events-registry.ts registers no expense describers, so both events are consumed with no effect. BASELINE_NOTIFICATIONS (access/baseline.ts:368 onwards) contains no EXPENSE_* rule. A NEXT_STEP assignment (finance or high-value), a withdrawal, a payment outcome and a reversal emit nothing. Reviewers only get the generic APPROVAL_REMINDER after 2 business days.
missing: The expense module sends no notices at all. Assigned manager, finance and high-value reviewers are not told about their task, and the claimant is not told about approval, return, rejection or payment status. DF12 (line 5011) requires these events: 'request submitted, assigned, approved, rejected, returned, withdrawn/cancelled ... expense final decision/payment operational status'. BR-033 says 'Notify assigned reviewer for pending decision and claimant for outcome'. Fix: add describers and events for every step and payment outcome, with dedupe keys per occurrence, plus mandatory in-app rules that use operational placeholders only (no reasons, receipts or payment identifiers).

brdQuote: limit delegated decisions to the approved period, request category and equivalent reviewer authority
exists: Delegation exists only in the database. There is the delegation table (db/migrations/0001_core_tenancy_org_access.sql:416-436: at most 30 days, no self-delegation, approver differs from delegate), approval_task.delegation_id with a foreign key to the delegate (0002:247-273), and the decision guard's expiry and delegator-self checks (0002:364-374). No service, route or engine code refers to delegation: there is no match for 'delegat' in apps/api/src or apps/web/src. createTask never sets delegation_id, and decideTask accepts only the task's assignee (workflow/engine.ts:172-180, 389).
missing: Delegated decisions are impossible. There is no API to create, approve, list or end a delegation, and nothing routes a delegator's tasks to the delegate. The rules are already fixed: DF03 (line 4911) sets inclusive/exclusive timestamps, a 30-day maximum, same company, action limits, no redelegation, and no Admin or confidential eligibility gained through delegation; DB018 (line 3030) says the 'delegate must hold applicable base permission and scope; original entitlement remains required'. Fix: build the delegation lifecycle with independent approval (the FR-067 grant pattern); let the delegate receive and decide tasks within the delegated permission and period; refuse delegations that would widen scope.

brdQuote: scoped claim, approval ageing, payable and reconciliation outputs
exists: EXPENSE_REGISTER (apps/api/src/modules/report/catalogue.ts:287-325) gives one row per claim by submission date: state, claimed total, approved, net paid, outstanding, payment state and currency. GET /expense/payables (expense/service.ts:470-487) is a JSON list with no age, and it is not an export. There is no other expense output; docs/08 run 10 lists 'expense reports/ageing (FR-079 outputs)' as not built.
missing: Missing outputs, all named in section 11 (line 2287: 'Claim/line register, approval ageing, category spend, payable ageing, payment reconciliation'): approval ageing (pending claims by step and reviewer, with age), payable ageing (approved unpaid or part-paid claims by age since approval), category spend, and a claim-line register. The reconciliation output also lacks the pending reservations and reversed amounts that DF07 reconciliation needs ('confirmed plus pending cannot exceed approved'). Each output should use the same scope predicate and period as its list. Columns still need section 11 owner approval before release (docs/03 I-40 item 12).

brdQuote: No matching or multiple equally applicable policies blocks submission
exists: Rule selection in submitClaim (apps/api/src/modules/expense/service.ts:277-282) orders matching rules by num_nonnulls(grade_id, location_id) desc and takes the first (limit 1). The unique index (0012_expense_payment.sql:71-72) allows a grade-only and a location-only rule for the same category. The employee's grade and location come from today's assignment (ea CTE, 235-236), not from the expense date.
missing: When two equally specific rules match, one is chosen arbitrarily instead of blocking with POLICY_AMBIGUOUS. Example: ACCOMMODATION rules for grade G1 and for location L1, both matching a G1 employee at L1; the same claim may or may not be flagged depending on the query plan. Fix: detect a tie at the highest specificity and refuse submission; evaluate the classification as at the expense date (DF06 'Apply the policy effective on the expense date'). Latent today, because no API creates such rules, but it becomes reachable once notify-8 is built.

brdQuote: delivery failure is visible and does not reverse an already committed business approval
exists: dispatchOutbox (apps/api/src/modules/notification/dispatcher.ts:580-593) retries a failing event after 1, 5 and 15 minutes, then sets outbox_event.failed_at and last_error and records outbox_event_attempt rows. GET /notifications/delivery (notification/routes.ts:106-117) lists only notification rows and their attempts. No route reads outbox_event or outbox_event_attempt.
missing: An event that fails to dispatch, for example through a describer or recipient-resolution error, creates no notification row, so support cannot see the lost alert through any route. Fix: add a permissioned, company-scoped listing of FAILED and retrying events to the delivery log, showing topic, occurrence time, attempts and error class but never the payload. This is a business delivery log, separate from the capacity metrics endpoint.

brdQuote: Proposed account deactivation and asset/document clearance depend on an owner-approved offboarding policy.
exists: Separation (apps/api/src/modules/lifecycle/exit.ts separateOne, lines 471-487) only changes the employee status to INACTIVE_SEPARATED. It does not touch role_assignment, user_account, user_employee_link or manager_assignment, and no migration trigger does either. resolveAccess (apps/api/src/modules/access/authorize.ts 113-148) checks that the user, company, assignment and role are active but never looks at the linked employee's status. As a result, a separated HR Administrator keeps COMPANY-scope confidential grants. A separated Reporting Manager keeps TEAM scope (the manager_assignment is still effective) and can still decide pending tasks; the approval_decision trigger (0002 lines 332-377) does not check employment status either. Reviewer selection treats the two paths differently. directManagerUser (workflow/engine.ts 113-130) requires the manager to be ACTIVE_PROBATION, ACTIVE_CONFIRMED or NOTICE. isEligibleReviewer, used for fallback lists (engine.ts 63-87, 132-146), has no employment-status check, so a separated HR Administrator on a fallback list keeps receiving new exit, withdrawal, settlement and leave tasks. docs/06 row 12 notes that account deactivation waits for an offboarding policy, but docs/03 has no owner question for it: I-31 covers held assets only and I-40 does not list it.
missing: An owner decision on the offboarding policy, recorded in docs/03 as an OPEN item. It needs to cover: whether and when a separated user's assignments end, which own-ESS access (payslips, letters) survives, and what happens to the separated person's pending tasks. Until then nothing stops separated users from being chosen as reviewers or acting with their pre-separation grants. A fail-closed interim can be built once the owner agrees: leave users whose only linked employee is INACTIVE_SEPARATED/ARCHIVED out of reviewer selection, and show their still-active assignments to access administrators.

brdQuote: no-data is distinguished from a failed query
exists: processReportQueue (apps/api/src/modules/report/service.ts 67-137) marks an execution FAILED only in three cases: the report is unavailable, access was revoked, or def.rows threw an HttpError. Any other error leaves the execution QUEUED, because the transaction rolls back. Examples: a statement timeout (57014; the worker runs outside any budget scope, so the 15 s pool default applies, db/pool.ts:32), an exception from toCsv/toXlsx (called outside the try; xlsx.ts throws plain Errors such as 'ZIP archive too large'), or a failed report_output insert. The worker always claims the oldest QUEUED row across all companies (service.ts 74-75). runScheduledJobs calls processReportQueue without settle (worker/scheduler.ts:143), so every tick claims the same execution again, fails again, and no later report or AUDIT_TRAIL export of any company is ever generated. There is no attempt count or backoff, and the RUNNING state is never used. The requester sees QUEUED indefinitely while the web polls every 3 s (pages/work.tsx 1233-1238).
missing: A generation failure must end the execution FAILED with an error class, after bounded retries like bulk jobs (1, 5 and 15 minutes, then FAILED). A failing execution must not block other reports. A test must cover a report whose rows() throws a database error and show it ends FAILED, distinct from COMPLETED with 0 rows.

brdQuote: configure view, create, amend, submit, approve, export, upload, process, lock and reopen rights separately for each module
exists: Two routes are guarded only by settlement.read.amount (apps/api/src/modules/lifecycle/settlement-routes.ts 222-259): GET /v1/settlements/:id/export (CSV/XLSX/PDF) and GET /v1/settlements/export-archive (a ZIP of up to 100 settlements with all amounts). That is the same grant every settlement reviewer and approver needs just to open a settlement. The settlement permission catalogue has only read, prepare, review, approve and release (db/migrations/0039_settlement.sql 257-263). Every other confidential export uses a separate export action: catalogue reports require <resource>.export (report/routes.ts:69), payroll run exports require payroll_report.export.amount (0069; I-45 cites FR-002/FR-066), and appraisal and training exports use their own export actions. docs/03 I-46 records the read grant without addressing FR-002.
missing: A separate settlement export right (for example settlement.export.amount, ceiling-only for the HR Administrator), checked by both export routes and re-checked inside the archive build. Reading a settlement for review would then no longer allow bulk export of compensation amounts. It needs a migration for the permission row and the role ceiling, and tests that a holder of settlement.read.amount without the export right gets 403 on both routes.

brdQuote: generate relieving and experience letters from approved exit data and applicable templates
exists: letterData (apps/api/src/modules/lifecycle/letters.ts 61-126) fills resignationDate and lastWorkingDate only when an APPROVED or SEPARATED exit exists. A placeholder is mandatory only if the template author does not list it as optional. Creating, saving and publishing a template (letters.ts 179-261) applies no rule by letter type; checkOptional only requires optional placeholders to be used. previewLetter and generateLetter (300-411) accept any published template on any employee process. RELIEVING and EXPERIENCE are seeded letter types (registration.ts 98-106). The tests in letters.api.test.ts pass only because their sample template happens to use {{lastWorkingDate}} as mandatory.
missing: Two rules for RELIEVING and EXPERIENCE letter types. First, publishing must require joiningDate and lastWorkingDate as mandatory placeholders. Second, preview and generation must require an approved or separated exit of the employee (for a clearance checklist, the process's own exit). Today a relieving letter can be produced for an active employee with no approved exit, or without the employment period (acceptance line 1041: 'The letter shows the approved employment period'). Tests are needed for both refusals.

brdQuote: no component already paid in monthly payroll is paid again in settlement
exists: Settlement lines are entered or uploaded by hand (calculation is NOT_CONFIGURED). checkLine (apps/api/src/modules/lifecycle/settlement.ts 192-217) checks only that the component is active, the sign, the line kind and the notice period. Monthly payroll pays a leaver through the approved last working date (payroll/calculate.ts 184-198: eligible_to = least(leaving_date, service_end)) and keeps one payroll_line per component (0043_payroll.sql 1182-1199). Nothing compares the two, so a final-month salary component can be paid by the processed monthly record and again as a settlement line. The settlement detail's reconciliation context (remainingBalances, settlement.ts 560-571) shows only leave balances and loans; it shows no salary arrangement and no payroll records for the final period.
missing: A rule, with a test, that a settlement line cannot repeat a component already paid by the employee's processed monthly payroll for the same service period, and the reverse: a later monthly run must not pay what an approved settlement already contains. The owner must define 'already paid' and say whether it blocks or only warns, because settlement lines have no service period (DB080) and docs/03 I-40 item 2 (how a settlement is paid) is still open. This acceptance criterion should be added to that owner item. A read-only panel of the payroll records for the final period can be built now.

brdQuote: after approval requires HR independent decision and history
exists: decideWithdrawal refuses APPROVE while any settlement revision is DRAFT, SUBMITTED, REVIEWED, APPROVED or RELEASE_ELIGIBLE, with the message 'cancel or finish it first' (apps/api/src/modules/lifecycle/exit.ts 337-339). Neither remedy exists for an approved settlement: only a DRAFT can be cancelled (settlement.ts 341-346), and APPROVED can only move to RELEASE_ELIGIBLE, which is terminal (0039_settlement.sql 228-253). Settlements can be prepared during the notice period (createSettlement accepts APPROVED exits), and requestWithdrawal does not check for them (exit.ts 178-209). So once a settlement is approved, the employee can still request a withdrawal that HR can never approve. markReleaseEligible (settlement.ts 467-489) also ignores a pending withdrawal request, unlike finalRelease (exit.ts 415-416) and the separation job (exit.ts 475-476).
missing: docs/03 I-29 refuses a withdrawal only after final release or after the last working date; the code adds an undocumented, irreversible cut-off at settlement approval. The owner must decide what an approved withdrawal does to a live settlement: void it with its history kept, or refuse withdrawal requests once a settlement is approved, with a clear error code at request time. Separately, release eligibility should wait for a pending withdrawal decision, as final release already does.
files: db/migrations (new, only if a voided settlement state is chosen)

brdQuote: dashboard counts reconcile to the queue
exists: The Reporting Manager widget 'Leave and expense decisions waiting' (apps/api/src/modules/dashboard/service.ts 278-286, widget at 283) uses MY_OPEN_TASKS (service.ts 103-109). That metric counts every PENDING approval_task of the user, of any kind and from any of the user's assignments. Managers also hold exit recommendation, timesheet approval, appraisal rating, attendance correction and work-request duties by default (lifecycle, timesheet and appraisal registrations; LEAVE_MANAGER in access/baseline.ts). The widget therefore shows more than the leave queue (/v1/leave/tasks) plus the expense queue (/v1/expense/tasks) in the decision inbox (apps/web/src/pages/work.tsx 532-575). F2 (BRD line 5096) defines this widget as 'Assigned leave/expense tasks'. No test reconciles it (dashboard.api.test.ts covers only own pending requests), although docs/06 says the dashboards reconcile with their source lists.
missing: A metric that counts only the manager's leave_request, leave_cancellation and expense_claim tasks (plus outdoor duty and holiday work if the owner counts them as leave), built from the same predicate as those queues (dashboard/tasks.ts myPendingTasks). It needs a test that the widget equals the sum of those queues' items. TREASURY_OPERATOR 'Assigned tasks' also uses MY_OPEN_TASKS and needs the same check.

brdQuote: Auditors can trace who changed an employee grade and which payroll run used it
exists: Payroll run membership is selected by the employee's grade at the service end (payroll/runs.ts 215-240, scope_grade_ids), but neither payroll_run_member (0043_payroll.sql 801-823) nor payroll_record (966-1023) records the grade or assignment that was used. Payroll run audits are run-level only (runs.ts 356, 540, 1062: counts, filters and totals, no employee ids). The assignment-change audit nests the grade inside the 'assignment' object (employee/changes.ts 152-168), and the audit viewer shows only top-level operational keys and never values (audit-trail/service.ts 47-52). An auditor therefore cannot tell a grade change from a department or location change. The AUDITOR baseline role has no employee-history or payroll read access (access/baseline.ts, AUDITOR entry).
missing: Record on the run member and the payroll record the employment assignment (or grade) the employee was selected and calculated with. Give the audit duty a read-only trace from an employee to the payroll runs and records that used each assignment or salary-arrangement revision (identifiers and dates only, no amounts). Name nested assignment fields, such as grade, in the audit trail's field list. Add a test that follows a grade change to the run that used it.

brdQuote: large exports run with visible progress and recoverable download links
exists: The report API offers only POST /v1/reports, GET /v1/reports/:id and GET /v1/reports/:id/download (apps/api/src/modules/report/routes.ts). There is no route that lists the requester's own executions. The web keeps requested ids in component state (pages/work.tsx 1155 and 1222: 'No reports requested in this session'), so a page reload loses every download link. The audit trail page requests AUDIT_TRAIL and tells the user to 'download it from Reports when it is ready' (pages/admin.tsx 33 and 70). The Reports page lists only reports requested on that page in the same session, so an audit export cannot be downloaded from the UI at all. The RUNNING state (0002_workflow_audit_files_imports.sql:568) is never set, nothing shows progress, and failures are shown as the raw failureCode (work.tsx:1244).
missing: GET /v1/reports: the caller's own executions in the same company and assignment, newest first, paged with a total, with state, row count, failure code and expiry. The Reports page and every page that requests a report should use it. Also needed: a RUNNING state or progress indicator during generation, readable failure texts, and tests.

brdQuote: list and export outputs use identical approved scope, period and filters
exists: The audit viewer filters by resource, recordKey, actorUserId, action and period (audit-trail/routes.ts 30-54; auditEventQuery in service.ts 35-60). The AUDIT_TRAIL export passes only from and to into the same query (report/catalogue.ts 661-706). The POST /v1/reports filter schema has no resource, recordKey, actor or action (report/routes.ts 36-57), and AUDIT_TRAIL declares no record filters. The export therefore always contains every company event in the period, and the web 'Export period' button drops the viewer's record filters (pages/admin.tsx 33).
missing: AUDIT_TRAIL should accept the viewer's filters: declare them as record filters, apply them through auditEventQuery, and keep them in the filter snapshot, so a filtered audit view and its export contain the same events. Add a test that the viewer total equals the export row count for the same filters.

brdQuote: sortable columns where appropriate
exists: Every paged list uses a fixed order chosen by its module: pageOf (apps/api/src/db/paging.ts 31-58) takes orderBy from the caller. No route schema in apps/api/src accepts a sort parameter (no sort or sortBy anywhere), and no web table offers column sorting. docs/03 records no decision about sorting.
missing: An allow-listed sort parameter (column key and direction, with a stable id tie-breaker) on the paged lists and report views where sorting is meaningful, such as the employee, exit, settlement, audit and team lists. It must be applied in SQL before paging so totals and pages stay consistent. The web needs sortable column headers. Add tests that paging stays stable under each sort.

brdQuote: optional uploaded-list selection
exists: The ZIP export selects settlements only by ids passed in the query string (apps/api/src/modules/lifecycle/settlement-routes.ts 234-259). There is no way to upload a list, such as employee codes, to search or select settlements. The comment on exportSettlementArchive (settlement.ts 816-822) calls this id selection the 'optional uploaded-list selection', while docs/03 I-46 lists 'selection driven by an uploaded list' as not built. The BRD field dictionary marks the uploaded-list search 'Import matching rules pending' (line 2025).
missing: Owner-defined matching rules for the uploaded list: key columns, handling of unknown or duplicate codes, and scope. After that, an upload that resolves to settlements and drives the list filter and the ZIP selection. Also correct the misleading code comment and add the open question to docs/03.

brdQuote: Proposed exact invoice/receipt reuse requires a recorded review; similarity alone cannot determine an automatic rejection.
exists: apps/api/src/modules/expense/service.ts submitClaim (lines 289-306) flags DUPLICATE_SUSPECTED, OVER_LIMIT, LATE_SUBMISSION and RECEIPT_MISSING and requires only the claimant's exception_reason (expense_line check constraint, db/migrations/0012_expense_payment.sql). On finance approval, decideExpense inserts expense_line_decision rows with `l.reason?.trim() || null` (service.ts 395-401). Trigger hrms_expense_line_decision_check (0012) requires a reason only when allowed_amount < claimed_amount. The approval_decision reason is optional for APPROVE. Test expense.api.test.ts:285 approves an over-limit line in full with only the claimant's reason.
missing: No authorised reviewer's documented clearance exists for a flagged line. A finance approval of a duplicate, over-limit, late or missing-receipt line at its full amount records no reviewer reason. This breaks FR-075 'clearance retains its reason' and DF06 (line 4951) 'financial Admin ... records a reason for reduction/rejection/exception'. Needed: require a non-empty reviewer reason on expense_line_decision whenever the line's exception_flags is non-empty (trigger plus service validation), show the flags in the finance decision form, and add tests for each flag kind.

brdQuote: Final entitlement approver cannot release the related claim payment.
exists: assertIndependentReleaser (apps/api/src/modules/expense/service.ts 669-674) refuses the preparer, the claimant and expense_obligation.approved_by. It is used by releasePayment, recordOutcome and reversePayment. decideExpense sets approved_by to the user who made the final APPROVED decision (service.ts 424-428). For a claim above the high-value threshold that user is the high-value approver. The finance approver who fixed every line amount (expense_line_decision) is never checked. The dashboard predicate independentOf in expense/metrics.ts repeats the same rule.
missing: On high-value claims, the finance reviewer who decided the reimbursable line amounts and final entitlement (FR-073) can release the payment, record its CONFIRMED or FAILED outcome, and reverse it (given payment.release/reverse grants, which sit in the same HR Administrator ceiling). Needed: treat every actor of an expense_line_decision on the claim's approved revision, plus the final approver, as entitlement approvers in assertIndependentReleaser and in metrics.ts. Add a test: the finance approver of a claim above 50,000 is refused at release.

brdQuote: Notify assigned reviewer for pending decision and claimant for outcome; other recipients require explicit scoped rule.
exists: expense/service.ts enqueues 'expense.submitted' (line 334) and 'expense.decided' (line 449). increment/service.ts enqueues 'increment.proposed' (line 212) and 'increment.decided' (line 340). notification/dispatcher.ts describe() has no case for these topics. modules/events-registry.ts registers no expense or increment describer. BASELINE_NOTIFICATIONS (access/baseline.ts) has no expense or increment decision template. So dispatchOutbox consumes these events 'without effect' (dispatcher.ts:265). The only increment notices are the INCREMENT_PROPOSAL_DUE and INCREMENT_DECISION_DUE reminders.
missing: No in-app notice is ever produced for any of these: an expense claim waiting for its manager; the finance and high-value step assignments (nothing is emitted at NEXT_STEP); the claimant's approved, returned or rejected outcome; an expense withdrawal (withdrawClaim writes neither an outbox event nor an audit record); payment status (prepare, release, outcome and reversal emit nothing); an increment proposal waiting for its approver; an increment decision. DF12 (line 5011) lists 'request submitted, assigned, approved, rejected, returned, withdrawn/cancelled ... increment review due/decision; expense final decision/payment operational status' as required events. Needed: describers and catalogue entries using operational placeholders only (never amounts), an event at each step assignment, and tests.

brdQuote: Late punches enter approved open-period amendment processing; locked historical results are not silently rewritten.
exists: biometric/sync.ts createPunch inserts a punch for any instant, however old. Daily processing in attendance/service.ts upserts attendance_record ('on conflict ... do update ... where not attendance_record.amended', around line 247) and only increments calculation_count. Neither POST /attendance/processing nor the ATTENDANCE_PROCESSING bulk kind (bulk/kinds.ts) checks whether the work date falls in a payroll period whose run is PROCESSED_LOCKED. payroll_record_lop (0043_payroll.sql:1109) references attendance_record_id and stores only units; no trigger protects referenced attendance records.
missing: After a late punch (or any input change), a rerun silently overwrites a daily result that a processed, frozen payroll record used as loss-of-pay evidence. The earlier derived result is not kept (only manual amendments are logged), and no exception or adjustment marker is raised. FR-022 requires the design to define payroll-lock dependencies. Needed: refuse reprocessing of results used by a processed run, or divert it into an attributable amendment that keeps the prior result and flags the difference for a later adjustment (adjustment valuation itself stays blocked under FR-100, per docs/06). Add tests.
files: db/migrations (new guard/history for attendance_record rows referenced by payroll_record_lop)

requirement: Financial integrity instruction (line 107); C5; DF07; ZT07; ZT15
brdQuote: Make request retries and payment outcomes idempotent.
exists: preparePayment (apps/api/src/modules/expense/service.ts 580-583) returns any existing instruction with the same idempotency_key as replayed:true (HTTP 200). It does this before checking the key's claim, amount or payment date, and before canAccessEmployee and reassertAccess. reversePayment (731-733) returns replayed:true whenever any payment_event has that event_key, including the instruction's own CONFIRMED event or another instruction's event, without checking the kind, instruction or amount. By contrast, workflow/engine.ts refuses a key used for another task (IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED), payroll input batches store request_hash and refuse reused keys with other content (0043:455), and recordOutcome checks the instruction.
missing: A reused key that carries a different request (another claim or amount, or a reversal whose key matches an earlier confirmation) is reported as already done while nothing is recorded, so the operator believes a payment or reversal exists. The replay path also reveals instruction state without a scope check. Needed: compare the stored request (claim via allocation, amount, payment date; or instruction, event kind and amount) and refuse mismatches with 409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED; check access before returning a replay; add tests.

requirement: Financial integrity instruction (line 103); BR-017; FR-072; FR-074
brdQuote: Keep claimant facts immutable after submission and retain all earlier versions and decisions.
exists: Lines are frozen per submitted expense_revision by the hrms_expense_revision_frozen and hrms_expense_line_frozen triggers (0012). The business purpose, however, is stored only in expense_claim.purpose (0012), and reviseDraft overwrites it (`update expense_claim set purpose = $3 ...`, expense/service.ts:160) when a RETURNED claim starts its next revision. expense_revision has no purpose column, the submit audit records only revision/total/lines, and reviseDraft writes no audit record.
missing: The purpose the manager reviewed in revision N (FR-072 'approve business purpose') is lost when the claimant revises a returned claim, so reviewers and auditors cannot see what was originally submitted. Needed: store purpose on expense_revision, frozen with it; read the current purpose from the current revision; backfill existing claims; add a test that revision 1's purpose survives resubmission.

brdQuote: Repeating the same receipt or invoice creates a review exception
exists: insertLines (expense/service.ts 54-56) fingerprints employee|expense date|category|amount|receipt checksum. submitClaim flags a duplicate on an equal fingerprint (same employee) or an equal receipt-file checksum (company-wide). expense_line.invoice_reference is stored (0012) but never compared and never returned by getClaim; merchant is not used either.
missing: Reuse of the same invoice (same merchant and invoice reference) is not flagged when it comes with a re-scanned or different receipt file, a different date, a split amount, or from a colleague. Such a line can be approved and paid twice. DF06 (line 4951): 'matching an external claim/reference key cannot create duplicate entitlement'. Needed: match normalised (merchant, invoice_reference) across live submitted claims company-wide as DUPLICATE_SUSPECTED, serialised with an advisory lock like the checksum key; show the reference to reviewers; add tests.

requirement: Financial integrity instruction (line 105); BR-024; FR-076; DF07; OQ-17
brdQuote: Use one approved expense obligation, even if the payout route is payroll. Maintain the same liability allocation ledger across routes.
exists: Expense payouts run only through the direct manual route: payment_instruction and payment_allocation against expense_obligation, with the conservation trigger (0012). Wave-2 payroll allows REIMBURSEMENT heads with calculation_basis INPUT (payroll_head_revision, 0043:37-74), and payroll_input lines (0043:498-528; payroll/inputs.ts) carry only a free-text reference. Nothing links a payroll reimbursement to an expense_obligation or counts it in expense_obligation_ledger. I-40 item 11 asks only about the reimbursement register's source.
missing: An approved claim can be reimbursed through a payroll input while still showing UNPAID with its full allocatable amount, so a second direct payment is possible (BR-024: 'changed route cannot create another entitlement'). DF07 (line 4959) excludes payroll reimbursement only for wave 1, OQ-17 lists the direct/payroll route for approval, and docs/03 records no wave-2 decision. The owner must decide whether payroll may settle expense claims. If yes, payroll reimbursement lines must allocate against the obligation ledger, with route changes limited to unpaid, unprocessed obligations. If no, payroll REIMBURSEMENT inputs must be barred from settling expense claims.

brdQuote: Missing or ambiguous policy blocks submission, rather than using a guessed default.
exists: submitClaim refuses a submission with no active policy (POLICY_NOT_FOUND) or lines under different policies (POLICY_AMBIGUOUS). Rule selection (expense/service.ts 277-282) uses `order by num_nonnulls(pr.grade_id, pr.location_id) desc limit 1`, so when a grade-only rule and a location-only rule both match, one is picked arbitrarily. The classification comes from the employment_assignment in force today (the `ea` CTE uses hrms_business_date(now)), not on the expense date. The only policy is the provisioned DEFAULT revision with company-wide rules (access/provision.ts 177-204). The expense routes only list and activate policies (expense/routes.ts 304-319), and no trigger freezes the rules of an ACTIVE policy. Leave, attendance and confirmation all refuse equal-specificity ties (leave/service.ts:49, attendance/service.ts:106, confirmation/service.ts:46).
missing: (1) HR cannot create dated expense policy revisions, category limits or grade/location rules (FR-078 'approved dated category policies, eligible employee classifications'; DF06 'configured, effective-dated review thresholds'). (2) Equally specific rule matches must be refused as POLICY_AMBIGUOUS instead of picking one. (3) Eligibility should use the employee's classification on the expense date. (4) Rules of an activated policy need a DB freeze so approved claims keep the rules they were decided under. Add tests for each.
files: db/migrations (freeze trigger for rules of ACTIVE policies)

brdQuote: Apply approved change once to salary history; later corrections use controlled attributable superseding events.
exists: increment_history (db/migrations/0011_salary_increments.sql 221-256) is append-only and unique per case and per new salary arrangement, with no supersedes or correction reference. The increment module offers only cycle, plan, proposal, off-cycle and decision actions (increment/routes.ts; service.ts proposeOffCycle and decideIncrement). No correction path exists anywhere in the module.
missing: An applied increment recorded with a wrong amount or date can only be offset by another ordinary off-cycle case. That counts as a second salary change with its own per-change percentage, not a correction: nothing marks the original as superseded, and the history and annual reports cannot select 'the approved effective chain' (DF14 line 5031: 'Correction retains original/superseding records'). Needed: a correction case with independent approval (as for off-cycle cases, DF15) that creates a superseding history record and arrangement revision linked to the original, with INCREMENT_HISTORY and ANNUAL_INCREMENT excluding superseded records. Arrears for locked periods stay blocked as recorded in docs/06.

brdQuote: Independent approved revision application rechecks row scope, base version, evidence and effective date.
exists: decideChange (sensitive-change/service.ts 429-480) re-checks the base, the evidence and the effective date at approval, and row scope through decideTask. A future-dated approval becomes SCHEDULED. applyDueChanges (service.ts 561-598) later applies it as the system user, re-checking only that the approval instance is APPROVED for the current revision and that the base still holds.
missing: At deferred application nothing re-checks that the approving assignment still holds sensitive_change.review.private with row scope over the employee (for example after a revoked grant, or a transfer out of the approver's scope), or that the evidence is still released and verified. The change applies regardless. Needed: in applyDueChanges, re-resolve the approver's assignment (resolveAccess plus canAccessEmployee) and the evidence status, ending in CONFLICT for re-approval otherwise; add tests.

brdQuote: Apply the C5 proposed expense lifecycle only after approval.
exists: withdrawClaim (expense/service.ts 460-467) allows WITHDRAWN only from DRAFT or RETURNED, and the transition catalogue (0012) has only those two withdrawal transitions. This follows C5 (line 4704): 'owner must confirm whether submitted withdrawal is permitted; deny until decided'. docs/03 records no owner decision on this or on the other C5 points ('withdrawals, line exceptions, reapproval and cancellation timing', line 4694).
missing: FR-074 ('permit withdrawal only before committed final approval or payment'; acceptance: 'simultaneous withdrawal/final approval yields one valid result') and DF03 ('Withdraw only before a final decision') expect a pending claim to be withdrawable, which the code refuses. The owner must confirm whether MANAGER_PENDING, FINANCE_PENDING and HIGH_VALUE_PENDING claims may be withdrawn, and record the decision in docs/03. If they may, building it means cancelling the active approval under lockTransaction, adding catalogue transitions, and testing the race against final approval.

brdQuote: Own approved masked bank summary; submitted full fields limited to owner and eligible reviewers
exists: GET /v1/employees/:id/sensitive-changes (apps/api/src/modules/sensitive-change/routes.ts:171-175) is guarded only by sensitive_change.read.private. This permission is in the HR Administrator ceiling separately from employee.read.bank (sensitive-change/registration.ts). listChanges calls present() (service.ts:643-668), which returns `proposed: sealed.proposed` unmasked for every request, including APPLIED BANK requests, whose proposal is exactly the bank detail in force. Only the `before` side is masked (shownBefore, service.ts:605-608). privateProfile() (service.ts:740-753) masks bank values unless the caller holds the bank group, and I-18 says previous bank values are masked even for reviewers. The test (sensitive-change.api.test.ts:187-192) checks masking only in the reviewer queue.
